title: PROTEUS: A Self-Evolving Red Team with Surface Expansion for Agent Skill Ecosystems
claim: An adaptive attacker agent iteratively mutates artifacts using audit and runtime feedback, guided by a graph of candidate composition chains.
layout: 3 blocks: top chain strip, bottom-left agent, bottom-right contract; feedback loop arrow
description: A boxed diagram in muted gray, with a salmon block for the agent. Along the top, a light panel holds five gray boxes joined by arrows: 47k skills, AST fingerprint extraction, rule graph plus theme similarity, budgeted BFS paths, and subgraph manifests with an LLM flow simulator. Its footer reads 'Output: ranked potential attack chains'. A bent arrow labeled 'Potential malicious chain' drops into the bottom-left salmon 'Red Team Agent' panel. That panel lists tool boxes such as read_skill, list_skills and submit_mutation, then a Pre-Flight self-check bar and stacked L1/L2/L3 levels (free discovery, path expansion, surface expansion). The bottom-right gray 'Greybox Round Contract' panel runs from a Blueprint funnel through three auditor slots (D1-D3) to audit findings F, then Sandbox, then Per-object Oracle. A 'Poisoned skill' arrow goes from the agent into the contract. A Feedback Quadruple box returns 'Round feedback' to the agent, closing the loop.
caption: \ours{} overview: graph-guided chain composition (top) feeds the red-team mutator agent (bottom-left), which interacts with the defender-agnostic greybox round contract (bottom-right) via a feedback quadruple $\langle b, \ell, F, R\rangle$.
abstract: Agent skills extend LLM agents with reusable instructions, tool interfaces, and executable code, and users increasingly install third-party skills from open marketplaces and repositories. Skills expose both executable behavior and context-setting documentation, so their deployment risk extends beyond one-shot audits and prompt-level red teaming: an attacker can use audit and runtime feedback to iteratively refine a malicious skill. We formalize this threat as adaptive leakage—the probability that a budgeted attacker produces a skill that passes vetting and causes verified runtime harm—and present PROTEUS, a graybox self-evolving red-team framework to quantify it. PROTEUS searches a five-axis skill-attack space through a unified audit->sandbox->oracle pipeline, using structured findings and runtime evidence to guide cross-round mutation. Path expansion searches alternative implementations of a retained variant's objective; surface expansion transfers structural motifs to different objectives. On the initial 20-seed grid across eight Phase-1 configurations, PROTEUS achieves 40-90% Attack Success Rate within five rounds (ASR@5), with positive learning-curve slopes against both public auditors. Phase-2 expansion produces 438 jointly bypassing and oracle-lethal variants: SkillVetter is bypassed at >=93% in every cell, and AI-Infra-Guard (AIG), the strongest evaluated auditor, admits up to 41.3% joint success. These findings show that single-shot skill vetting substantially underestimates residual deployment risk against adaptive attackers. Code: https://github.com/SJTU-iBDS-Lab/proteus.
